name: LM1117MP-3.3
title: LM1117: 800 mA low-dropout linear regulator, fixed and adjustable
summary: The LM1117 is a positive linear regulator for loads up to 800 mA, with 1.2 V dropout at full load. It comes in fixed 1.8, 2.5, 3.3 and 5.0 V versions and an adjustable version (1.25 V reference, 1.25 V to 13.8 V out) in SOT-223, TO-220, TO-252, TO-263 and WSON-8, with current limiting and thermal shutdown. It needs at least 10 µF of tantalum on its output. LM1117MP-3.3 is the 3.3 V, 0 to 125 °C version in SOT-223.

circuits.title: 1.25 V to 10 V adjustable regulator with improved ripple rejection
circuits.description: The adjustable part sets its output with a 121 Ω resistor from VOUT to ADJ and a 1 kΩ variable resistor from ADJ to ground, so VOUT = 1.25 × (1 + R2/R1). A 10 µF capacitor sits on the input and 100 µF on the output. The capacitor from ADJ to ground is optional; fitting it raises ripple rejection.

circuits.title: Basic adjustable regulator
circuits.description: The part holds VREF (1.25 V) across R1, from VOUT to ADJ. The current through R1, plus the small adjust-pin current, flows on through R2 to ground and sets VOUT = VREF × (1 + R2/R1) + IADJ × R2. 10 µF on the input, 100 µF on the output.

circuits.title: Fixed output regulator with line resistance to the load
circuits.description: A fixed part feeds a load through wiring with resistance Rt1 in the output lead and Rt2 in the return. The load sees VLOAD = VOUT – IL × (Rt1 + Rt2), so each lead's drop subtracts from the regulation at the load; the load is best connected directly at the VOUT and ground terminals.

circuits.title: Adjustable regulator wired for best load regulation
circuits.description: R1 connects right at the output pin, not at the load, so the output lead's resistance Rt1 is not multiplied by (1 + R2/R1). R2's lower end returns to the load's ground side, past the return resistance Rt2, which senses ground at the load. VLOAD = VREF × (R1 + R2)/R1 – IL × Rt1.

circuits.title: Regulator with protection diode
circuits.description: An adjustable regulator with a 10 µF capacitor from ADJ to ground and 100 µF on the output. An optional 1N4002, anode at the output and cathode at the input, carries the output capacitor's discharge current when the input is shorted; it is recommended where 1000 µF or more sits on the output and the input can be shorted to ground instantly.

circuits.title: Fixed output regulator
circuits.description: Any fixed version with a 10 µF tantalum capacitor on the input and another on the output. The input capacitor is required when the regulator sits far from the supply's filter capacitor.

parts.note: tantalum; required if the regulator is far from the supply filter

circuits.title: Adjusting the output of a fixed regulator
circuits.description: A 5 V part with its ground pin lifted through a 1 kΩ variable resistor, bypassed by 10 µF, so the output can be set from 5 V to 10 V. Input above 12 V, 10 µF on the input, 100 µF on the output.

circuits.title: Regulator with reference
circuits.description: A 5 V part whose ground pin stands on a reference diode, so its output sits above the reference: 7.5 V out, with the 2.5 V reference node brought out as a second output. Input above 9.0 V, 10 µF on the input, 100 µF on the output.

circuits.title: 5 V logic regulator with electronic shutdown
circuits.description: R1 = 240 Ω and R2 = 720 Ω set 5 V. A 2N2219 from the ADJ node to ground, driven from a TTL line through 1 kΩ, shorts ADJ to ground when turned on, which pulls the output down to about 1.25 V. Input capacitor 10 µF tantalum, output capacitor 100 µF.
notes: With the transistor on, the output is about 1.25 V.

circuits.title: Battery backed-up regulated supply
circuits.description: Two 5 V parts share one output. The line-fed part, behind a series diode, has its ground pin raised by 50 Ω, so the output sits at 5.2 V while the line is present. A second diode and a 1 kΩ resistor charge a 6.5 V battery, which feeds the second part; on battery the output is 5.0 V. The 1 kΩ value sets the charge rate.

circuits.title: Low dropout negative supply
circuits.description: A transformer and bridge rectifier make a floating supply; a 5 V part regulates it with its output tied to system ground, so its ground pin and the rectifier's negative side sit at –5 V. 10 µF across the rectified input, 100 µF across the output.
notes: The transformer input is floating.

circuits.title: Power dissipation diagram
circuits.description: The currents that set dissipation: IIN enters at VIN, IL leaves VOUT into the load, IG leaves the ground pin, with IIN = IL + IG. The part dissipates (VIN – VOUT) × IL + VIN × IG.

operation.text: A positive linear regulator for up to 800 mA with 1.2 V dropout at full load. Fixed outputs of 1.8, 2.5, 3.3 and 5 V, and an adjustable version settable from 1.25 V to 13.8 V with two resistors. A Zener-trimmed bandgap reference holds the output within ±1 %. Current limiting and thermal shutdown are built in.

LM1117 parts are specified for junction temperatures of 0 to 125 °C, LM1117I parts for –40 to 125 °C. The TLV1117 is offered as a later pin-compatible replacement, and the TLV761 as a drop-in for the fixed SOT-223 versions.

The adjustable part holds 1.25 V between VOUT and ADJ. That voltage across R1 sets a constant current that flows on through R2 and so sets the output. The adjust pin's own current, about 60 µA, is small and stable over line and load, so its error is usually negligible. The fixed versions have R1 and R2 inside.

The part regulates the voltage between its output and ground (or adjust) pins. Lead resistance between the part and the load adds to the load-regulation error, so the load should connect directly at the VOUT and ground terminals. On the adjustable part R1 goes right at the output pin, and R2's ground end can go to the load's ground for remote ground sensing.

No protection diode is needed in normal use. On the adjustable part the internal resistance between ADJ and VOUT limits current, even with a capacitor on ADJ, and ADJ survives ±25 V transients measured from the output. A short from input to ground lets the output capacitor dump its charge back through the part; the internal output-to-input diode takes microsecond surges of 10 A to 20 A. With 1000 µF or more on the output and an instantaneous input short, add an external diode from output to input.
Fit a capacitor at the input; 10 µF tantalum serves nearly every case.

A capacitor from ADJ to ground keeps the ripple from growing with the gain the divider adds at higher output settings, raising ripple rejection. Its impedance at the ripple frequency must be below R1. When it is used, the output capacitor rises to 22 µF tantalum.
The output capacitor sets stability. The minimum is 10 µF tantalum, with ESR between 0.3 Ω and 22 Ω; more capacitance only improves stability and transient response.

Dropout rises with output current and changes with temperature; the input must stay above VOUT plus dropout over the whole current and temperature range, with margin where possible, and below the maximum input rating.

Load-current traces wide; the VOUT-to-ADJ feedback path as short as possible; the ADJ bypass capacitor right at the IC; any output-to-input protection diode close to the IC pins. On the WSON, pins 2, 3 and 4 are joined, and pins 5, 6 and 7 are joined, and the thermal pad is soldered down.

Thermal shutdown protects the part, but the junction must stay within 0 to 125 °C in operation. Work out PD, the allowed rise TJ(max) – TA(max) and from them the largest RθJA allowed, then pick package and copper area from the thermal tables and curves. The SOT-223 and TO-252 figures were measured on a set of test patterns with copper on top, bottom or split between the two sides, the tab soldered to the top copper.

Heat goes from the junction through the die and die attach to the lead frame, case and board, and on to ambient. RθJC depends on the lead frame, number of conducting pins, die size, die attach and moulding compound; RθJA also on the mounting pad, board, traces, nearby heat sources, air volume and ambient temperature. Case temperature is taken where the leads meet the mounting pad.
